subject: Literacy
title: The sounds /t/ and /p/
subtopics: Which sound do you hear first?
objectives: Children will hear and say the sounds /t/ and /p/ at the start of words.
Children will tell /t/ from /p/ with support.
content: Listening for the sounds /t/ and /p/ at the start of words and telling which sound they hear first.
teachingActivities: Say /t/ and /p/ as short, crisp sounds with no vowel added; /t/ is made with the tongue behind the teeth and /p/ with the lips; hold a tissue in front of your mouth to show the puff of /p/; keep the sounds clean and brief.
learnerActivities: Hear and say /t/ and /p/ at the start of words and tell /t/ from /p/ with support.
resources: A tap picture, a tin, a toy tiger
A pot, a pan, a pen
assessment: Observe whether each child says /t/ and /p/ clearly and points to the correct picture for each sound.
expectedOutcomes: Points to the right picture for /t/ or /p/.

lessons.title: The tap says t, t, t
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will hear and say the sound /t/ as the dripping tap sound.
successCriteria: Says the sound t when shown the tap
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can hear and say /s/ and /a/ and find objects that start with them.
lessons.starter: Hold up the tap picture and say "A dripping tap goes t, t, t." Tap your finger softly in the air.
teacherActivities: Say "t, t, t" in short crisp sounds with your tongue behind your teeth. Show your mouth.
Say "t, t, t" together while you tap the table gently.
Let each child look in the mirror and say t.
learnerActivities: Children watch your mouth and listen.
Children say "t" and tap their finger.
Children copy a soft quick t.
Child watches their mouth and says t.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Say "t, t, t" in short crisp sounds with your tongue behind your teeth. Show your mouth. Children: Children watch your mouth and listen.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "t, t, t" together while you tap the table gently. Children: Children say "t" and tap their finger.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "t" softly and quickly. Children: Children copy a soft quick t.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child look in the mirror and say t. Children: Child watches their mouth and says t.

practical.title: Dripping tap
steps: Give each child a finger to tap on their hand.
Say t, t, t with each tap.
practical.safety: Keep taps soft and do not let children tap hard on tables. Use a damp cloth for any water drips.

differentiation.support: Tap the child’s hand softly and say t together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a friend what the tap says.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Can you tap and say t?

lessons.conclusion: Turn off the pretend tap with a last quiet t.
lessons.homeConnection: Listen to a dripping tap at home and say t, t, t.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "hear and say the sound /t/ as the dripping tap sound" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: The tap says t, t, t. Drip, drip, drip.

lessons.title: The pot says p, p, p
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will hear and say the sound /p/ as the popping sound.
successCriteria: Says the sound p when shown the pot
Feels the puff of air on a hand
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can hear and say /s/ and /a/ and find objects that start with them.
resources: A pot or a picture of a pot
lessons.starter: Hold up the pot and say "Popcorn is popping in the pot. p, p, p." Make a popping sound with your lips.
teacherActivities: Say "p, p, p" in short pops. Hold a tissue in front of your mouth and let it move.
Say "p, p, p" together and hold a hand in front of the mouth.
Let each child look in the mirror and say p.
learnerActivities: Children watch the tissue move.
Children feel a puff on their hand.
Children copy a soft p and a loud p.
Child watches their lips and says p.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Say "p, p, p" in short pops. Hold a tissue in front of your mouth and let it move. Children: Children watch the tissue move.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "p, p, p" together and hold a hand in front of the mouth. Children: Children feel a puff on their hand.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "p" softly and loudly. Children: Children copy a soft p and a loud p.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child look in the mirror and say p. Children: Child watches their lips and says p.

practical.title: Popping corn
steps: Give each child a scarf to hold.
Pretend to be popcorn popping and say p, p, p.
practical.safety: Use only pretend popcorn and do not use real popcorn due to choking risk. Keep jumps small and soft.

differentiation.support: Hold the child’s hand and feel the puff with them.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to pop a pretend popcorn and tell a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Can you feel the puff?
questions.expected: Child says yes or shows the hand.

lessons.conclusion: Put the lid on the pot and say a last p.
lessons.homeConnection: Pop pretend popcorn with your child and say p, p, p.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "hear and say the sound /p/ as the popping sound" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: The pot says p, p, p. Pop, pop, pop.

lessons.title: Tin, tap, pot, pan
lessons.subject: Literacy
lessons.subtopic: Which sound do you hear first?
objectives: Children will hear whether a word starts with t or p.
successCriteria: Points to the t picture or the p picture
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can hear and say /s/ and /a/ and find objects that start with them.
resources: Picture cards: tin, tap, tiger, pot, pan, pen
Two baskets, one for t and one for p
lessons.starter: Show the two baskets and say "One is for t and one is for p. Listen for the first sound."
teacherActivities: Say "tin" and stress the first sound "t-in". Put the tin in the t basket.
Say "pot" and stress the first sound "p-ot". Put the pot in the p basket.
Say a word and let a child choose the basket.
learnerActivities: Children listen and say t.
Children listen and say p.
Child chooses the t or p basket.
Children sort the cards with support.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Say "tin" and stress the first sound "t-in". Put the tin in the t basket. Children: Children listen and say t.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "pot" and stress the first sound "p-ot". Put the pot in the p basket. Children: Children listen and say p.
Step 3. Teacher: Say a word and let a child choose the basket. Children: Child chooses the t or p basket.
Step 4. Teacher: Continue with all six cards. Children: Children sort the cards with support.

practical.title: T and p baskets
steps: Put two baskets on the mat.
Each child picks a card and says the word.
Put the card in the t or the p basket.
practical.safety: Use large soft cards and supervise sorting. Make sure each child has a turn.

differentiation.support: Say the first sound loudly and show the card for the child to place.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a new t or p word in the room.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What sound does tin start with?
What sound does pot start with?

expectedOutcomes: Sorts pictures by first sound t or p with support
lessons.conclusion: Count the cards in each basket and say t and p.
lessons.homeConnection: Say a word and ask your child if it starts with t or p.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "hear whether a word starts with t or p" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: The t and p song
lessons.subject: Literacy
lessons.subtopic: Which sound do you hear first?
objectives: Children will sing a song about t and p and do the matching actions.
successCriteria: Sings or hums the t and p song
Does tap or pop for each sound
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can hear and say /s/ and /a/ and find objects that start with them.
lessons.starter: Say "t, t, t" and tap. Say "p, p, p" and pop. Ask "Which one is it?"
teacherActivities: Sing "Tap, tap, tap says t, t, t. Pop, pop, pop says p, p, p." Show the cards.
Sing again and do a tap action for t and a jump for p.
Say a sound and let children do the action.
Let a child lead and choose t or p.
learnerActivities: Children listen and look at the cards.
Children copy the tap and the pop.
Child taps for t and pops for p.
Child leads and friends follow.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sing "Tap, tap, tap says t, t, t. Pop, pop, pop says p, p, p." Show the cards. Children: Children listen and look at the cards.
Step 2. Teacher: Sing again and do a tap action for t and a jump for p. Children: Children copy the tap and the pop.
Step 3. Teacher: Say a sound and let children do the action. Children: Child taps for t and pops for p.
Step 4. Teacher: Let a child lead and choose t or p. Children: Child leads and friends follow.

practical.title: Tap and pop game
steps: Sit in a circle with the two picture cards.
Say t or p and children tap or pop.
Change the order faster each time.
practical.safety: Keep jumps small and soft. Clear the floor and rest if children are tired.

differentiation.support: Do the action together and say the sound loudly.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose a sound and lead the game.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do for t?
What do we do for p?

expectedOutcomes: Tells t from p with actions
lessons.conclusion: Sing the song once quietly and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Play tap and pop at home: tap for t, pop for p.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sing a song about t and p and do the matching actions" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Tap, tap, tap says t, t, t. Pop, pop, pop says p, p, p.

lessons.title: Week 3 t and p check
lessons.subject: Literacy
lessons.subtopic: Which sound do you hear first?
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child hears and says /t/ and /p/.
successCriteria: Points to the right picture for t or p
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can hear and say /s/ and /a/ and find objects that start with them.
lessons.starter: Say t and p and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: t sound, p sound and sorting.
At each station say a word and ask "Is it t or p?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child says the sound or points.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: t sound, p sound and sorting. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station say a word and ask "Is it t or p?" Children: Child says the sound or points.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: T and p stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use large soft cards.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use two pictures.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to sort all six cards alone.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: says /t/ clearly; says /p/ clearly; tells /t/ from /p/ with support.

questions.question: What sound does tap start with?
What sound does pan start with?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 3
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye with a t and a p.
lessons.homeConnection: Play listening games with t and p at home.

What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
